lines.text: Wren told me the story afterwards, the way she tells everything. Short, and with far too much about arrows.
This stone marked the edge of the Pale when my father hunted here. It's a mile inside the ice now.
So the Pale moved?
The Pale moved.
And everything that lived in it was running. Elk, foxes, frost-wolves. All running south, straight past the hunters, as if they weren't even there.
That's not normal, is it.
Nothing that runs from wolves runs with wolves, Dunn.
Then the trees broke apart.
Argh!
Wren said she didn't think. She just shot.
One arrow. Through the eye.
Ow. Ow! Did you see that? I think it liked me.
Shut up and hold still.
That was when they saw him. A man painted white, standing between the frozen trees, with a spear in his hand.
You killed the white bear. Good. It would have followed you home.
Who are you?
Kell. Of the Skeld. The people of the White.
You are hunters from the warm valley. The one where the snow is melting.
How do you know about that?
Everyone in the White knows. The animals know. That is why they are running toward it.
Go home, hunter. Tell your warm lord this.
The White is waking.
You're coming with us. You can tell him yourself.
They turned for home that same night, with a stranger, a dead bear's claw, and Dunn complaining the whole way.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter twenty-three, coming soon.
